title: Curriculum started
text: Every earlier attempt at proper walking had to find balance, alternating steps and forward progress at once, and settled for a shortcut each time: skipping with one leg as a prop (v3, v4, v5-warm), stumbling forward with alternating steps and falling (v5-fresh), or standing still (v6). The curriculum gives each skill its own training reward: 1 balance, 2 step (alternating feet, even in place), 3 walk, 4 walk fast. Each stage starts from the previous stage's champion. Attempt 1 started Wednesday 08:15. Running alongside for comparison: v7-alt, which starts from the alternating stumbler and has to learn balance while walking.

title: v7-alt stopped; the curriculum gets the whole machine
text: v7-alt (warm start from the alternating stumbler, with the per-distance gait tax) kept alternating, with foot 2 leading about 52% of the time and roughly 15 front-foot changes per episode, but after 177 generations every training episode still ended in a fall around x = 14. It is kept below as a comparison but no longer trains, so the curriculum runs alone on the four cores. The local dashboard on port 8771 now follows whichever curriculum stage is active.

title: Attempt 1 found a shortcut: tapping in a split stance. Attempt 2 started.
text: Stage 1 of attempt 1 passed, but its champion balances with its feet 2.9 units apart, foot 2 always in front: the skipper's stance. Stage 2 then learned to tap its feet alternately in that stance: about 70 alternating touchdowns per episode and zero front-foot changes, so the feet never pass each other, and the search has stopped exploring (σ 0.013). Attempt 2 fixes both: stage 1 now also pays for keeping the feet together, and stage 2 only counts a touchdown as a step when the foot coming down is the front foot and the legs alternate. Under the new step reward the tapper drops from 105 to 47 points while a real stepper can earn about 300. Attempt 1 keeps running as the baseline.

title: Attempt 1 stopped; attempt 3 starts stepping from the stumbler
text: Attempt 1's stepping stage never stopped tapping: for over 200 generations it made zero front-foot changes, with its feet split almost one unit apart, and its search had stopped exploring, so I stopped it at generation 454. I also found that the plateau watcher had quit at 08:29 because it didn't know about the curriculum scripts; it's fixed and running again. Attempt 2 is still in its balance stage: no falls, body level, but the feet are 0.53 units apart and the pass test wants under 0.4. With the freed cores, attempt 3 skips balance and starts the real-steps stage from v5-fresh, the one walker that already swaps its feet about 17 times per episode. It only has to learn not to fall while stepping.

title: Attempts 2 and 3 stuck on opposite sides; attempt 4 adds training wheels
text: Attempt 2's stepping stage chose to stand still with its feet together: about one front-foot change per episode, because a step that falls costs more than standing earns. Attempt 3 did the opposite: it kept the alternating stumble, with about seventeen front-foot changes, but fell on all twenty test tracks at x ≈ 17, through both the step and the walk stage. Both were stopped. Attempt 4 uses training wheels: an upright torque on the body that keeps it from tipping, faded out over four stages (support 2, 1, 0.5, then none), followed by walking fast in the real game. With support 2 the stumbler never falls. Eighteen generations in, the best candidate already makes about eighty real crossing steps in an episode, foot 2 leads about 59% of the time, and it walks forward. The real test is whether the gait survives as the support is removed.
